lines.say: A quote is a promise about cost, made before the job exists.
lines.show: A quote is a promise about cost, made before the job exists.

lines.say: Every quote has four parts. Material, labor, setup, and margin.
lines.show: Every quote has four parts: material, labour, setup and margin.

lines.say: Material comes from the bill of materials, scrap included, at today's cost.
lines.show: Material comes from the bill of materials, scrap included, at today's cost.

lines.say: Labor is hours times a shop rate, not the wage. The rate must recover overheads.
lines.show: Labour is hours times a shop rate, not the wage. The rate must recover overheads.

lines.say: Now the trap. Margin and markup are different numbers.
lines.show: Now the trap. Margin and markup are different numbers.

lines.say: Example. On a cost of one forty two, a thirty five percent markup gives one ninety two. A thirty five percent margin gives two eighteen.
lines.show: Example: on a $141.99 cost, a 35% markup gives $191.69. A 35% margin gives $218.45.

lines.say: Spread setup over the real batch, or small batches lose money.
lines.show: Spread setup over the real batch, or small batches lose money.

lines.say: For most small job shops, quote where jobs and stock live, so each quote meets its real cost.
lines.show: For most small job shops, quote where jobs and stock live, so each quote meets its real cost.
